speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Prime Minister what are the plans under consideration to (i) encourage locally incorporated tech companies to choose the Singapore Exchange (SGX) over foreign stock markets for their Initial Public Offerings (IPOs), especially if they have been backed by local agencies during the start-up phase and (ii) to attract more investors with risk appetite for investing in start-ups to invest in new IPOs or tech companies currently listed on the SGX.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The challenge of sustaining a vibrant and attractive cash equities market is not unique to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Globally, the number of initial public offerings (IPOs) and proceeds raised has been declining since 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This was driven by the trend of companies staying private for longer and, more recently, against the backdrop of a challenging global macro-environment and interest rate environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In the first half of 2023, global IPO proceeds fell by 36%, while Asia Pacific IPO proceeds were down by 40%.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Many stock exchanges are also dealing with the trend of local companies looking to list on large overseas markets like the United States (US).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For instance, the United Kingdom (UK)’s largest chip design firm ARM Holdings recently listed in the US.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Yet, many of its companies list in the US due to its deep and liquid capital market and investor base.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Nearer to home, Hong Kong is also looking to retain and attract more IPOs amidst the more challenging macro-economic environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX has also been actively seeking cross-border partnerships with the regional exchanges to enhance its attractiveness as a gateway for Singapore companies and international investors to access regional capital markets and opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Overall, our initiatives aim to provide a more enabling environment for companies to consider listing on SGX.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: At the same time, Mr Speaker, Sir, we recognise that there are limits to how these measures can directly influence listing decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Companies considering possible public listings have several commercial objectives in mind.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In some cases, these considerations may prompt them to explore listing venues outside of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: First, they may decide to list in jurisdictions where they can secure the best valuations for their shareholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For quite a number of companies, a US listing is attractive due to the US’ deeper pool of investors and liquidity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Second, companies may list in jurisdictions that give them better exposure to their own target markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For example, a company planning to expand its business in China may choose to list in either Hong Kong or China, or both.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If we take an overly prescriptive approach by making Government support to promising startups conditional on a local listing, we may end up imposing a rule that may be at odds with the growth plans of the company or the founder.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Similarly, global investors who are in Singapore will ultimately determine how to allocate their capital based on their strategies and how they view the market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: So, again, if we prescribe that they must invest certain amounts in only locally listed companies, we will effectively constrain their investment mandates and end up losing a larger pool of investors who adopt a regional or a global view.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: In addition, MAS has a grant scheme which defrays listing costs for issuers listing on Catalist.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Apart from accessing public markets, private equity and venture capital, or PE/VC in short, have in recent years been an increasingly important source of growth capital for promising startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: More PE/VC managers have established their presence in Singapore and are coming in at earlier stages, which broadens the range of financing for our startups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS recognises the value of an attractive equities market as part of our overall financial services ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: That is why the Government and SGX have in place a range of initiatives to better position our equities market.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We will continue to monitor the situation closely and review and update our measures, where necessary, to adapt to the shifts in global capital markets.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: First, I do not think the question was asking for the grants to be conditional upon making these firms list in Singapore on SGX or Catalist, as appropriate.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Rather, it was just to get a sense of how many of these firms are receiving grants or support from the various agencies and how many of them eventually decide to exit via an IPO strategy and then, subsequently, decide upon careful consideration that they want to list elsewhere, as the Minister of State shared in his reply.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And does MAS then track the reasons why and what are the tensions between having a tech firm or just any startup decide to base themselves in Singapore, avail themselves of our grants and then, subsequently say, "Oh, actually, we rather have access to funds elsewhere" or "we rather try to access the capital markets elsewhere"?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I think having MAS to actually understand these tensions and the reasons why it is a good idea to be here but not a good idea to raise funds here and whether or not MAS does any studies to find out.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Once you find out the reasons why, it will eventually become easier to amend or to support our regulatory environment and regime to address some of the concerns that these startups will have, with the ultimate aim of making our SGX and our equities and capital market regime here in Singapore more active and, of course, deepen that pool in the market here.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: A related supplementary question is: does SGX and various agencies track the number of locally incorporated and home-grown tech startups which eventually, on a yearly basis, decide to list and go for an IPO here in Singapore?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If so, can the Minister of State share the data?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think her idea is to help and we are all aligned if we want to enhance our equities market.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That is the simple answer to the question.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I mentioned earlier on in my reply, we are doing all that we can to help to boost the equities market, but there is also a limit.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Because, ultimately, firms will have major commercial considerations, including valuations, including market, as well as including whether they can secure the best kinds of valuations elsewhere as well as whether they want to list in the market where they are closer to the particular target market.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If you ask any of the companies or firms, they will tell you that it is primarily a commercial decision.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Of course, we will do what we can.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On a broader perspective, I would like to share with the House also that in line with our Industry Transformation Map 2025, particularly on the financial sector, we are constantly looking at ways in which to enhance and deepen our financial sector.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The financial sector is not focused on just having an equities market.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We have a very vibrant foreign exchange market, we have a very vibrant wealth management market, we are into green finance, we are into fintech and others also.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, it is a dynamic, deep and also very diversified financial market.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just two supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I understand the Minister of State's point about it being a commercial decision for private companies to choose where they want to list.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: But I was just wondering: what is the Government's position, as to a ruling, such as that in Indonesia, whereby I believe the local companies can seek a dual listing, but they must also list on the local exchange?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second supplementary question is: on top of listings, there is also the broader issue of delisting in the local market.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And it is something which has been a challenge for the last couple of years, where the number of delistings has been more than the listings.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As a result, there are concerns as to whether or not this issue of perceived weaker valuations and lower liquidity could continue to result in a bit of downward spiral.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, just wondering in terms of the delisting part, what is the Government's approach towards addressing some of these issues?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will try to answer the second question first, which is regarding our delisting.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I mentioned in my main reply, there are a variety of different reasons why companies would list on a particular exchange, and also a variety of reasons why they would delist.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That is based upon maybe how they view the market, whether they want to list overseas, or they look at prevailing options.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They might want to go back to private, for example.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, there is a whole different variety of why they would want to do so.
